name: Adze-Titan
description: Adze-Titan is a massive gas giant whose atmospheric features look as though they have been hewn from raw cloud material by some titanic tool. The cloud bands are not the smooth, flowing ribbons seen on most jovian worlds but rather rough-edged, textured formations with sharp boundaries and angular storm systems that give the planet a carved, deliberately shaped appearance. A dark debris ring encircles the equator like a belt of stone chips, the remnants of a moon that ventured too close and was ground to fragments by tidal forces.

The planet dominates the inner system with its gravitational presence, shepherding asteroids and influencing the orbits of every other body. Its magnetic field is intense and irregular, with pole positions that wander across the cloud tops in patterns that have defied prediction for decades. The perpetual storms generate electromagnetic emissions across the full spectrum, creating a constant radio roar that drowns out weaker signals and makes communication in the planet's vicinity a constant challenge.

A navigation beacon maintains position in a stable Lagrange point, serving as a critical waypoint for ships transiting the system. The beacon requires frequent maintenance due to the electromagnetic environment, and its service crews are among the highest-paid technical workers in the sector. Adze-Titan's moon system includes fourteen bodies of varying size, several of which show signs of geological activity driven by tidal heating, making them objects of scientific interest in their own right.

The fuel reserves in Adze-Titan's atmosphere are estimated to be the largest in the sector, but the irregular magnetic field and the electromagnetic noise make skimming operations exceptionally hazardous. Automated skimmers have proven more successful than crewed vessels, but even they suffer a high attrition rate. The planet's gravitational influence makes it impossible to bypass, and every ship that transits the system must reckon with the Titan, navigating its debris ring, its radiation, and its storms with the respect that a world of this magnitude demands.
